title: Construction of localized extension on strict coefficient systems
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ have topology $J$, let $U\in\mathcal C$ and let $B:\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Sh}(J,\mathrm{CommRing})$. Assume module sheafification on $J$ and $J/U$ in a common coefficient universe with its locally bijective characterization. The SliceSystemExtensionPresentation $B,U$ of [def-sf-semilinear-slice-scalar-data] exists. Thus the actual localized extension $j_{B_n!}$ at each level extends to an additive functor from strict systems on $\mathcal C/U$ to strict systems on $\mathcal C$, whose transitions send every original summand $[x]_f$ to $[t(x)]_f$. Its object and map identifications are with the actual localized extension functors.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), 03EK (tensor product of module sheaves) and 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); the coefficient-generator refinement in lem-sf-semilinear-slice-scalar-generators.

proof.text: The normalized localized-extension adjunction unit is the original direct-sum summand followed by sheafification. Transpose a slice transition followed by the restricted level-m adjunction unit under the level-n extension adjunction. Restriction to the slice commutes sectionwise with scalar restriction. The transpose sends [x]_f to [t(x)]_f.

Adjunction injectivity and the unit formula show that original extension summands detect maps. Compare the identity transition and composite transition using the identity-on-sections scalar restriction unit and compositor. The original system identity and composition give equality on every summand. The same calculation with a system morphism proves the transition square for componentwise extended maps. Functor laws and additivity hold componentwise.
